chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Murazam ibn Hakeem, from the one who raised it to him, said:

Al-Harith al-Awar came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! I would love for you to honor me by eating with me.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him, 'On the condition that you do not exert yourself for me in anything.' And he entered. So Al-Harith brought him a piece of bread, and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) began to eat it. So Al-Harith said to him, 'I have dirhams with me,' and he showed them, and they were in his sleeve. 'So if you permit me, I will buy something for you other than this.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him, 'This [bread] is from what is in your house.'
ai.seo_question: What is the story of Imam Ali's simple meal with Al-Harith al-Awar?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s preference for *sunnah* simplicity over ostentatious hospitality, emphasizing that the essence of honor lies in the sincerity of the host rather than the extravagance of the meal. By accepting a simple piece of bread and rejecting the offer to purchase finer food, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) demonstrates that true generosity is rooted in contentment and avoiding unnecessary burden (*takalluf*) on the host. This narrative serves as a practical guide for social interactions, encouraging modesty and preventing the social pressure often associated with competitive feasting.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Murazam Bin Hakeym, from the one who raised it to him, said,

‘Harsa Bin Al-Awr came over to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! I would love it if you<sup>asws</sup> could honour me by eating with me’. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Upon the condition that you would not make efforts for me for anything’. And he<sup>asws</sup> went over. So Al-Haris gave him<sup>asws</sup> a piece of bread, so Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> went on to eat it. So Al-Haris said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I have some Dirhams with me’, and he went on to show these, and these were in his sleeve, ‘So if you<sup>asws</sup> were to allow me, I would buy something for you other than this’. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘This here is from what was in your house’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Murazim ibn Hakim from the one who has narrated it in a marfu‘ manner saying the following:

“Harith al-A‘war once came to ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and said, ‘O ’Amir al- Mu’minin, I wish you grant me the honor of having food with me. ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, said, ‘I accept your invitation, provided, that you do not overburden yourself by acting formally’. He (the Imam) went to his house. Harith brought a piece of bread and ’Amir al-Mu’minin began to eat. Al-Harith said, ‘I have a few dirham’ and he showed them. They were in his sleeves. ‘If you give permission I like to buy something for you besides these pieces of bread.’ ’Amir al- Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘This is what is in your house (so it is sufficient).”’
